newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Lion tax charge hits full year result.
newsitem.headline: Lion tax charge hits full year result.

text.p: Brewing company Lion Nathan Ltd said on Thursday earnings from operations rose 8.1 percent to NZ$246.6 million in the year to August 31, but it took a $74.2 million tax charge following a $1.8 million credit in the previous year.
Operating earnings from the Australian Brewing operations fell 2.8 percent to A$243.4 million, while market share eased to 42.0 percent from 43.4 percent last year.
New Zealand Liquor operating earnings rose 4.1 percent to $119.7 million, while market share was stable at 54.0 percent versus 54.4 percent last year.

In China, Wuxi Brewery operating earnings of $2.3 million, up from $1.2 million, contributed to an overall $0.2 million loss from China Brewing operations after corporate and market development costs. This compared with a $3.4 million prior year loss.
Lion said it reduced its operating loss from softdrinks to $5.1 million from $5.4 million previously.
The $74.2 million tax charge included $21.1 million of non-recurring tax following the conclusion of the 1985-90 New Zealand income tax audit.
Net earnings after abnormals and tax fell to $150.4 million from last year's $199.4 million.
Lion said it repaid NZ$146.4 million of debt, reducing balance sheet gearing to 69 percent from 79 percent.
